title: CORTET: Robust generation of simulation-ready tetrahedral meshes of the fetal cerebral cortex
summary: Every human brain folds differently, and such natural variation confounds the search for imaging biomarkers of neurodevelopmental disorders. Physics-based simulation can help determine the causal mechanisms that underpin this variability. Yet every simulation must be initiated from a volumetric mesh of the brain's interior, tetrahedral or hexahedral, and it is the worst element in that mesh, not the average, that decides whether the simulation runs at all.
